findings.title: CVE-2024-12345 timing attack vulnerability has been FIXED
findings.description: The authentication module at dashboard/server/middleware/auth.js properly implements timing-safe comparison using crypto.timingSafeEqual() to prevent timing attacks on API key validation.
findings.remediation: No action required - fix already implemented at line 44-64

findings.title: Development mode allows unauthenticated API access
findings.description: When NODE_ENV=development and API_KEY is not set, the auth middleware allows all API requests without authentication. This is intentional for development but must be documented.
findings.remediation: Ensure API_KEY is always set in production deployments. Current behavior is acceptable for development.

findings.title: Password reset token returned in API response
findings.description: The POST /api/users/:id/reset-password endpoint returns the reset token directly in the API response. In production, this should only be sent via email.
findings.remediation: Implement email delivery for password reset tokens instead of returning in API response. Line 1055 has a comment acknowledging this.

findings.title: User ID generation uses Math.random()
findings.description: User IDs are generated using Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure. While user IDs are not secrets, using crypto.randomBytes would be more robust.
findings.remediation: Consider using crypto.randomBytes() or UUID v4 for user ID generation. Current implementation is acceptable for non-security-critical identifiers.

findings.title: Password reset token uses Math.random()
findings.description: Password reset tokens at users.js:1036 use Math.random() instead of crypto.randomBytes(). Reset tokens should be cryptographically secure.
findings.remediation: Replace Math.random().toString(36) with crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') for reset tokens. Use the existing generateToken() utility from security.js.

positive_findings.title: Timing-safe API key comparison
